title: The compromised privileged account — question explanation
learningObjective: Prioritize containment, credential revocation and trusted recovery after suspected compromise
format: 16:9 educational motion-graphics video; narration; separate captions; no autoplay with sound
visualStyle: Deep navy and charcoal; restrained cyan/electric-blue highlights; limited purple accents; clean typography; purposeful, low-motion transitions; accessible contrast.

scenes.name: Scenario setup
scenes.visual: A privileged administrator reports a suspicious login. Audit records show a new session and unfamiliar mailbox forwarding rule. The user’s password may be compromised.
scenes.direction: Show a fictional simulated setting. Use generic UI and no actual organization, brand, user identity, credential, real URL or live account.

scenes.name: Learning objective and risk cue
scenes.visual: Prioritize containment, credential revocation and trusted recovery after suspected compromise
scenes.direction: Highlight only observable cues and explain the decision context without implying certainty beyond the scenario.

scenes.name: Recommended response
scenes.visual: Option D: Coordinate incident response: contain access, revoke affected sessions/tokens, secure credentials and recovery factors, preserve evidence, and investigate persistence. Account compromise requires coordinated containment and recovery, not only a password change.
scenes.direction: Animate the recommended defensive choice as a clear decision path. Display the action verb and trusted channel/control.

scenes.name: Why the other options fail
scenes.visual: Option A: Deleting evidence can obstruct investigation and may remove only visible indicators. Option B: Password change alone may leave active sessions, tokens, forwarding rules or attacker persistence in place. Option C: A broad disruptive response without scope assessment may cause unnecessary outage and is not proportionate.
scenes.direction: Show each unsafe alternative separately with a complete, concise reason. Do not depict operational exploitation, malicious code or credential capture.

scenes.name: Defensive takeaway
scenes.visual: Activate the incident-response process, coordinate identity and system owners, contain the affected account, preserve evidence and verify recovery before restoring access. After suspected credential compromise, address sessions, tokens, recovery paths and persistence as well as the password.
scenes.direction: Close with one readable takeaway and the next safe action. Keep the final frame long enough for comprehension.
